description: A clock generator and clock multiplier or divider driven from a display, four outputs each with their own ratio

params.text: With no cable in CLK it sets the tempo in beats per minute; with a clock patched it chooses the ratio from a list running from divide by 64 to multiply by 64. Inside SETUP it moves through the choices
Held down for about two seconds it opens or closes SETUP; inside SETUP a short press moves to the next setting, and outside it starts and stops the generated clock

inputs.text: The clock this module follows; with a cable here the module multiplies or divides it instead of generating its own tempo. A rising edge is counted above 1.7V and the input rearms below 0.2V
With a clock patched at CLK this sets the ratio, -5V to 5V covering divide by 64 to multiply by 64; with no clock patched it is a trigger that starts and stops, or resets, the generated tempo

outputs.text: The first output, at whatever ratio and pulse shape SETUP gives it
The second output, at whatever ratio and pulse shape SETUP gives it
The third output, at whatever ratio and pulse shape SETUP gives it
The fourth output, at whatever ratio and pulse shape SETUP gives it; SETUP can turn this one into a sine, triangle or sawtooth at the clock rate instead of a pulse

notes: the maker has retired this module: the README points to KlokSpid MkII in the OhmerPrems plugin as its replacement, and says no more work will be done on this one
almost every setting is inside SETUP, reached by holding the button down, and is read and changed on the display with the encoder rather than from the panel or the right-click menu
SETUP sets the output level for all four jacks together: 5V, 10V, 11.7V, which SETUP prints as +12V, or 2V
the CV input is read as -5V to 5V by default, and SETUP can switch it to 0V to 10V instead
with a cable in CLK the module is a multiplier or divider; with none it free-runs at its own tempo, and the display says which of the two it is doing

inputs.0:
high above 1V · stepped · one channel only

a negative voltage does nothing here.
inputs.1:
±5V · stepped · one channel only

a negative voltage subtracts from the knob.
